name: Magnetism and magnetic effects of current

questions.q: Which of the following materials is classified as ferromagnetic and is strongly attracted to magnets?
What is the direction of magnetic field lines outside a bar magnet?
a: From the South pole to the North pole
From the North pole to the South pole
In concentric circles with no direction
Radiating outward in all directions from the center

questions.q: What occurs when two like magnetic poles (such as North and North) are brought close together?
a: They neutralize each other magnetism completely.

questions.q: What name is given to a long coil of wire carrying an electric current that produces a strong, uniform magnetic field inside it?
How can the strength of the magnetic field inside an electromagnet solenoid be increased?
a: Increasing the current flowing through the coil or adding an iron core
Decreasing the number of turns of wire
Using plastic wire instead of copper

questions.q: What rule is used to determine the direction of the magnetic field around a straight current-carrying conductor?
What is the primary difference between a permanent magnet and a temporary electromagnet?
a: Electromagnets are made of hard steel, while permanent magnets are made of soft iron.
Permanent magnets lose their magnetism when cold.
Electromagnets can be switched on and off by controlling the electric current, whereas permanent magnets retain their magnetism indefinitely.
Permanent magnets have only one pole.

questions.q: Why is soft iron commonly used as the core of an electromagnet rather than hard steel?
a: Soft iron melts at higher temperatures.
Soft iron is much cheaper to manufacture.
Soft iron retains its magnetism permanently after the current is switched off.
Soft iron magnetizes and demagnetizes easily and quickly when the current is switched on and off.

questions.q: What happens to a current-carrying conductor placed at right angles to a magnetic field?
a: It experiences a mechanical force acting perpendicular to both the field and the current.
It heats up and melts instantly.
It aligns parallel to the magnetic field lines.

questions.q: Which rule is used to find the direction of the force acting on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field (the motor effect)?
Which of the following factors will increase the magnitude of the force on a current-carrying wire in a magnetic field?
a: Reducing the strength of the magnetic field
Increasing the current or strengthening the magnetic field
Lengthening the wire parallel to the field lines

questions.q: What is the function of the split-ring commutator in a direct current (DC) electric motor?
a: To increase the voltage supplied to the motor
To reverse the magnetic field of the permanent magnets
To supply electricity directly to the stationary brushes
To reverse the direction of current in the rotating coil every half-turn, ensuring continuous rotation in one direction

questions.q: What term describes the production of an electromotive force (emf) or electric current in a circuit when it experiences a changing magnetic field?
According to Faraday Law of Electromagnetic Induction, what increases the magnitude of the induced emf in a coil?
a: Decreasing the speed of the magnet movement
Increasing the speed of movement, the number of turns in the coil, or the strength of the magnetic field

questions.q: What does Lenz Law state regarding the direction of an induced current?
a: The induced current flows in the same direction as the magnetic field.
The induced current creates zero magnetic effect.
The induced current always flows in such a direction as to oppose the change producing it.
The induced current cancels out the original voltage.

questions.q: What is the primary function of a step-up transformer in an electrical power transmission system?
a: To increase the current and decrease the voltage
To convert alternating current into direct current
To eliminate all electrical resistance in cables
To increase the voltage and decrease the current to reduce energy loss over long distances

questions.q: Why do transformers require an alternating current (AC) input rather than a direct current (DC) input?
a: AC creates a continuously changing magnetic field in the primary coil, which is necessary to induce an emf in the secondary coil.
AC travels faster through copper wire.
Direct current cannot pass through coils.

questions.q: What is the formula that relates the primary voltage (Vp), secondary voltage (Vs), primary turns (Np), and secondary turns (Ns) in an ideal transformer?
a: Vp times Vs = Np times Ns
Vp plus Vs = Np plus Ns

questions.q: An ideal transformer has 200 turns on its primary coil and 800 turns on its secondary coil. If the primary voltage is 50 V, what is the output voltage on the secondary coil?
Why are laminated iron cores used in practical transformers instead of solid iron blocks?
a: To make the transformer lighter in weight
To reduce energy losses caused by induced eddy currents circulating within the core

questions.q: What happens when a magnet is pushed rapidly into a closed coil of wire connected to a center-zero galvanometer?
a: The galvanometer needle deflects momentarily, indicating an induced current.
The needle spins continuously in one direction.

questions.q: Which of the following devices converts electrical energy into mechanical rotation using the motor effect?
What is the purpose of the slip rings connected to the rotating coil in an alternating current (AC) generator (alternator)?
a: To maintain continuous electrical contact with the rotating coil while allowing the external circuit to receive AC
To increase the magnetic field strength

questions.q: How can you determine the magnetic poles of a current-carrying solenoid?
a: By using the right-hand grip rule, where fingers curl in the direction of conventional current and the thumb points to the North pole

questions.q: What is magnetic induction?
a: The process where an unmagnetized magnetic material becomes temporarily magnetized when placed near or in contact with a permanent magnet
The creation of sound waves from magnets
The flow of electrons through a vacuum

questions.q: Which of the following materials is classified as non-magnetic?
What is the main advantage of transmitting electrical power at very high voltages across the national grid?
a: It reduces the current in the transmission lines, significantly decreasing thermal energy loss due to resistance (I squared R losses).

questions.q: If an ideal transformer has a primary voltage of 240 V and a secondary voltage of 12 V, and the secondary current is 5 A, what is the primary current?
What happens to iron filings sprinkled around a bar magnet?
a: They form patterns that map out the shape and direction of the magnetic field lines.
They repel each other into straight vertical lines.

questions.q: What is the function of the carbon brushes in a DC electric motor?
a: To maintain electrical contact between the external power supply and the rotating commutator

questions.q: What term is used to describe a region of space where a magnetic material experiences a magnetic force?
What does a cathode-ray oscilloscope display when connected to the output terminals of a simple AC generator being rotated by hand?
a: A straight horizontal DC voltage line
A sinusoidal alternating voltage waveform varying with time

questions.q: Which of the following describes hard magnetic materials such as alnico or steel?
a: They are difficult to magnetize initially, but once magnetized, they retain their magnetism permanently.
They cannot be used to make magnets.

questions.q: How does the strength of the magnetic field change as you move further away from a long straight current-carrying wire?
What is the key difference in construction between a DC motor and an AC generator?
a: A motor uses slip rings, while a generator uses a split-ring commutator.
A DC motor uses a split-ring commutator to feed current in, whereas an AC generator uses slip rings to extract induced alternating current.
A generator requires no external movement.

questions.q: What happens when a bar magnet is cut in half into two smaller pieces?
a: One piece becomes a pure North pole and the other becomes a pure South pole.
Both pieces lose their magnetism completely.
Each resulting piece becomes an independent magnet with its own complete North and South poles.
